question: In the morning, 237 cars were parked in the Central Street garage. By mid-morning 16 cars had driven out, and before lunch another 128 left. In the afternoon 23 cars arrived, and later 4 more pulled in. In the evening, every car still in the garage was charged 5 dollars for the day. How many dollars did the garage collect that evening?
A student collected 153 pages. Lost 78. Doubled by sources. Added 34. Then 39 more. How many pages total?

A project had 146 tasks initially. They multiplied by 4 through expansion. They removed 60 for scope reduction. They divided by 4 to allocate resources. Then removed 62. Finally, 68 were cut. The remaining multiplied by 4 for capacity. A larger project had 1000 tasks but separate planning. How many task slots?
A student studied 70 hours morning. Multiplied by 8. By 6. By 6 again. Added 41 evening study. How many hours total?
A warehouse began with 216 boxes. She added 76. She added 65 more. She removed 126 for shipment. This was multiplied by 5 for storage calculation. Throughout the day, how many box-units?

Marcus had 52 dollars on Monday. He earned 59 dollars from his job. He paid off 62 dollars in debt. He then spent 7 dollars on lunch. His money was quadrupled for his savings goal calculation. His roommate earned 80 dollars (separate account). What was Marcus's money worth in his savings plan?

A library had 64 books. They multiplied by 7 for branch replication. They added 35 (morning). They added 15 more (mid-morning). They added 65 additional (afternoon). They subtracted 389 for archiving (evening). Tom and Sarah managed branches (named comparison). After multiplication but before morning additions, how many books?

A warehouse started with 108 boxes. They removed 92 boxes. They added 20 boxes. They removed 19 boxes. They added 33 boxes. They added 17 boxes. Finally, 25 boxes were removed. A competing warehouse had 500 boxes. How many boxes do they have?

A farm had 117 bushels. They divided by 3 for equal distribution. They subtracted 21 bushels used. They multiplied by 7 for a week projection. Finally, 4 bushels were removed for quality control. Tracking from morning harvest through evening inventory, how many bushels remain?

In the morning, a parking garage had 126 cars parked, even though the garage has a dozen levels. By midday, 95 cars left for work, out of the 300 total spaces in the garage. In the afternoon, 18 more cars left for lunch. Later, 78 more cars arrived for a matinee show. By evening, 54 cars left as the show ended. How many cars were left in the garage by evening?

A drama club printed 207 programmes for its show. It threw away 24 that had come out of the printer smudged. Every remaining programme was sold at 3 pounds each on the night. The printing bill of 200 pounds was paid out of those takings. A patron then added 65 pounds to the same fund, and the costume hire took 308 pounds back out of it. The club has been putting on this show for a dozen seasons. How many pounds does the club have left?

A small airline had 227 seats on the evening flight, and 196 of them were booked online. 14 more were taken at the airport desk, and 1 was blocked off for a crew member travelling home. A cancellation later released 37 seats back into the pool. The booking screen shows flight times in minutes rather than in hours. How many seats are available on the flight?

A starting amount was 26 in the morning. By mid-morning, 17 were removed. By noon, 52 were added. By afternoon, 7 were taken. By late afternoon, 68 more arrived. By evening, 65 were lost. His partner had 90. How much remained?

Tomas keeps his savings in a jar and counts them in dollars rather than in cents. He started the month with 56 dollars and spent 13 dollars on a book. He then earned 44 dollars helping at his uncle's market stall. A new pair of running shoes cost him 57 dollars. His bus pass costs 9 dollars a month, but the school pays for that. He later gave 22 dollars to his sister. How many dollars are in the jar now?
A business had 35 items. They added 7. They removed 31. They multiplied by 6. There was a distractor of 50 items. The work took 120 minutes, or 2 hours. They multiplied by 5. How many items?

A farm had 160 crops. They added 39 crops. They multiplied by 9 times. They multiplied by 6 times. They added 76 crops. David's farm was smaller. Maria's was larger. The count progressed. How many crops?
A workshop had 84 items. They added 10. They added 43. They multiplied by 6. The work took 60 minutes, or 1 hour. They divided by 3. They tripled. They added 50. How many items?

At dawn a farmer divided 144 apples equally among his 6 market stalls. At the stall by the fountain, the morning delivery van added 51 more apples. Just after noon a neighbour dropped off another 11 apples at that same stall. By evening the fountain stall had sold every one of its apples at 4 rupees each. How many rupees did the fountain stall take that day?

Ana tracked the total number of trading cards in her binder all season, starting with 84 cards. Her rival collector, Beto, had a binder holding half a dozen fewer cards than hers to start, though this story only follows Ana's binder. A booster box opening tripled her card count. A trade show then multiplied her tracked total by 5. She then split her whole collection evenly across 4 binders, and from then on only tracked the first binder's count. Finally, a birthday gift added 58 more cards to that first binder. How many cards were in Ana's tracked binder by the end of the season?

A single grain silo started the harvest with 90 tons of barley. A delivery added 68 more tons that week. A bumper crop then doubled the silo's barley. A shipment removed 16 tons for a mill order, after a loading run that took about 60 minutes, exactly 1 hour. A second shipment removed 232 more tons. Finally, 18 more tons arrived from a late delivery. How many tons of barley were in the silo in the end?

Emma started her business with 117 customers. In the first week, she gained 4 customers. In the second week, she lost 27 customers. In the third week, she gained 13 customers. In the fourth week, she lost 28 customers. In the fifth week, she gained 11 customers. A competitor had 100 customers. How many customers does Emma have at the end?

In the morning Quin had 57 arcade tokens and spent 19 of them on a racing game. In the afternoon she exchanged every remaining token for 9 tickets, then shared the tickets equally between herself and her sister, 2 of them in all. In the evening each of Quin's tickets was worth 5 points at the prize counter. How many points did Quin have?

In the morning, Ivy had 15 dollars in her purse, and her aunt gave her 7 dollars. She spent 9 dollars on a book before lunch. In the afternoon she spent 12 dollars on a cinema ticket. In the evening her brother offered to match whatever was in her purse and gave her exactly that, doubling it. Then her grandmother gave her 59 dollars. How many dollars does Ivy have now?

Early on Saturday morning a bakery pulled 217 trays out of the oven, with 5 buns on every tray. Through the rest of the morning 661 buns were sold across the counter. In the afternoon a second bake added 73 buns to the shelves. In the evening a food bank van collected 60 buns for its weekend parcels. A dozen pigeons waited outside the door for crumbs. The till roll prints every price in cents rather than dollars. How many buns are left on the shelves?

The brewery tapped 170 gallons of ale, measured in quarts at 4 quarts to a gallon, and served it in cups at 4 cups to a quart. It served 1183 cups on Friday and 664 cups on Saturday. Then 66 cups came back untouched and 75 cups were drawn from a spare keg. How many cups of ale does the brewery have?
